test_title: PYST 39: SSC GD Constable 2025 - Quantitative Aptitude (Held On: 21 Feb, 2025 - Shift 3)
subject: maths
question: Bipin offers a discount scheme that on buying 7 notebooks, get 3 for free. What will be the sale price (in ₹) of a notebook with a marked price ₹185, if the equivalent percentage discount is applied?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

In a Buy X Get Y Free scheme, Discount % = Free Items ÷ Total Items × 100

Equivalent Discount % = 3 ÷ (7 + 3) × 100 = 30%

Sale Price = (100% − 30%) of Marked Price

Sale Price = 0.70 × 185 = 129.50

**∴ The correct answer is ₹129.50.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 
 

 Total = 10 Notebooks
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 

 7 Paid Notebooks
 
 

 3 Free Notebooks
 
 
 Equivalent Discount = (3 ÷ 10) × 100 = 30%

**Given:**

⇒ Free items = 3

⇒ Paid items = 7

⇒ Marked Price (MP) of 1 notebook = ₹185

**Formula Used:**

⇒ Equivalent Discount % = [Free items ÷ (Paid items + Free items)] × 100

⇒ Sale Price (SP) = MP × (100 − Discount%) ÷ 100

**Calculation:**

⇒ Equivalent Discount % = [3 ÷ (7 + 3)] × 100

⇒ Equivalent Discount % = (3 ÷ 10) × 100 = 30%

⇒ Sale Price of 1 notebook = 185 × (100 − 30) ÷ 100

⇒ Sale Price = 185 × (70 ÷ 100)

⇒ Sale Price = 185 × 0.7

⇒ Sale Price = 129.50

**∴ The correct answer is ₹129.50.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Buy X Get Y Free

The effective discount is always calculated on the total number of items received (X + Y), not just the paid items. Discount % = Y ÷ (X + Y) × 100.

Successive Discounts

When multiple discounts are given sequentially (e.g., a% and b%), the effective single discount is calculated as: D = a + b − (a × b ÷ 100).

Marked Price & Selling Price Relation

Selling Price (SP) is obtained after deducting the discount from Marked Price (MP). SP = MP − Discount = MP × (100 − Discount%) ÷ 100.
